findings.title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP.
findings.comment: The unpasteurized juices in the display cooler in the lobby were observed to not have a Consumer Advisory label on them. The PIC stated that they ran out of labels and they are expected to get more by Tuesday. A follow up is scheduled for 10/26/2026 to ensure that each bottle of unpasteurized juice has the warning notice as follows: “WARNING: This product has not been pasteurized and, therefore, may contain harmful bacteria that can cause serious illness in children, the elderly, and persons with weakened immune systems.” In the event of running out of labels in the future, ensure that there is a back-up option to communicate this warning notice to consumers.
findings.citation_text: 3-404.11(B) Treating Juice. Juice packaged in a food establishment shall be: (B) Labeled, if not treated to yield a 5-log reduction of the most resistant microorganism of public health significance: (1) As specified under § 3-602.11, and (2) As specified in 21 CFR 101.17(g) Food labeling, warning, notice, and safe handling statements, JUICES that have not been specifically processed to prevent, reduce, or eliminate the presence of pathogens with the following, “WARNING: This product has not been pasteurized and, therefore, may contain harmful bacteria that can cause serious illness in children, the elderly, and persons with weakened immune systems.”

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: There was a personal bag observed to be on the top of a container of ginger in the kitchen cooler. The PIC was informed and moved the lunch bag away from the ginger. It is recommended to have a container in the bottom of the cooler labeled “Personal” for employee food and drinks. Ensure that personal items are in a designated area away from food-contact surfaces and food items to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no measurable concentration of sanitizer in the sanitizer bucket at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) remade sanitizer to an approved concentration (400 ppm quaternary ammonia). Ensure sanitizer is made (and tested using facility’s test strips) at a frequency to have the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a wet sanitizing cloth on the prep table. Wet textiles left out may lead to the growth and harborage of microorganisms. Ensure sanitizer cloths are stored in a sanitizing solution in between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the facility to be lacking sanitizer test strips that correspond with the solution used for sanitizing. Chlorine (Cl) test strips were found in the facility, however quaternary ammonia (quat) is the sanitizing solution currently being utilized. The facility should either use Chlorine bleach as a sanitizer, or obtain quat test strips, to ensure sanitizer can be tested for the correct concentration. The inspector gave some quat strips to the facility, however a spot check will occur on 09/22/25 to ensure the facility has obtained their own.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the freezer drawers to contain a significant amount of food debris. Debris on nonfood contact surfaces poses a potential to contaminate ready to eat (RTE) food items. Ensure the drawers are cleaned routinely to prevent cross contamination of RTE food items.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
This location is attempting to sample the juices without any form of hand washing available at the stand. The sampling was discontinued for the event. A follow-up should be conducted at next weeks market to ensure proper sampling procedures are taking place. Multiple suggestions were given including setting up a temporary hand washing station and pre-packaging the samples in the store prior to transporting to the market.

6/18/25 (Repeat) This location is attempting to sample the juices without any form of hand washing available at the stand. The sampling was discontinued for the event. A follow-up should be conducted at next weeks market to ensure proper sampling procedures are taking place. Multiple suggestions were given including setting up a temporary hand washing station and pre-packaging the samples in the store prior to transporting to the market.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
No person in charge was present during this inspection. Ensure a designated person in charge is trained and present at all times of operation. 
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No CFM was present during this inspection. Facility must be under the direct supervision of an on-site CFM during all times of food prep and service. Ensure sufficient CFMs are on staff and scheduled to cover all shifts.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Blender pitchers are cleaned in the small sink in the front area after each use, and are sanitized at the end of each day. Discussed procedures with staff. Ensure blender pitchers are sanitized and air-dried at least every 4 hours during continuous use.
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
A pan of chicken was observed in the top of the prep cooler with a date of 10/7. Staff indicated that the chicken was thawed on that date. A second pan of chicken was observed in the bottom of the prep cooler without any date-marking. CORRECTED- The 10/7 chicken was voluntarily discarded. The unlabeled chicken should be discarded if staff do not know when it was thawed.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
The ice scoop in the ice machine was observed with the handle in contact with the ice. Ensure the scoop is stored with the handle extending out of the ice to prevent bare hand contact with the ice and to prevent contact between the handle and the ice. The ice scoop was moved so the handle is out of the ice.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single-service spoons accessible to customers were observed mixed directions (handles and spoon ends up). Ensure utensils are stocked handles-up to prevent hand contact with the food contact ends of the utensils. CORRECTED- Staff rearranged the utensils upon request.
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. [C]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Unlabeled spray bottle of clear liquid observed under the smoothie counter. CORRECTED- PIC labeled bottle to indicate its contents (sanitizer).
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]
